newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes flat vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes flat vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed almost unchanged against the dollar as the market looked as if it had flattened out ahead of U.S. elections, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.09 against the U.S. unit after opening at 57.08, moving little in either direction, they said.
"The rupee has been at the 57.10 level for about a week and a half and the market is getting the feel that the Central Bank is happy with these levels," said a Standard Chartered dealer.
On Tuesday, the Central Bank reduced the U.S. currency only by 0.20 local cents and fixed buying and selling at 55.9647 and 57.0953, respectively.
"I would say the market should be at these levels for the next two weeks or so," the Standard Chartered dealer said.
The market was also awaiting the outcome of the U.S. presidential election, a Hatton National Bank dealer said.
"The Central Bank rate will certainly be guided by what happens in the U.S. market," the dealer said.
Overnight call money, which opened at 16 percent, closed at 14 percent with the market very liquid.
